afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 072300
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
400 PM MST Mon Sep 7 2026

.UPDATE...
Updated Aviation

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Above normal temperatures will prevail starting Tuesday resulting 
in widespread moderate Heat Risk and areas of major Heat Risk.

- Extreme Heat Warnings will begin Tuesday for portions of the lower 
deserts.

- Mostly quiet weather conditions are expected for the first half of 
the week, then chances for thunderstorms increase across central and 
eastern Arizona during the latter half of the week.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
The RAP40 500MB analysis and GOES WV imagery continue to show the 
subtropical ridge positioned over northwestern TX, a large trough 
over NW CONUS. The Desert SW sits between these two features with a 
feint stream of upper level moisture being advected into the western 
lower deserts resulting in a few light showers/virga early this 
morning and lingering upper level clouds.
   
Ensembles remain in good agreement that the subtropical high will 
begin to shift westwards, peaking over the Desert SW by mid week 
with H5 heights between 594-597 dam. 500 MB heights at this level 
are near climatological maximum values for the time of year. This 
will lead to afternoon temperatures 4-5 degrees above normal, 
resulting in temperatures between 105F-111F. Overnight lows will 
also provide very little relief as the lingering cloud coverage 
mentioned earlier will hinder radiative cooling, and dew points are 
expected to be well into the 60s across much of the forecast area 
and locally into the lower to middle 70s for areas such as the Lower 
CO River Valley and Imperial Valley. With all of these factors taken 
into consideration Major HeatRisk will make a return to most of the 
region tomorrow and even more widespread by Wednesday, with the 
overnight lows being the main driver as they are flirting with the 
record warm lows through the end of the work week. As a result, 
Extreme Heat Warnings have been issued for portions of the lower 
deserts staring on Tuesday (starting Wednesday for Lower CO River 
Valley, Desert Center, and La Paz County). 

Little to no chance for showers/thunderstorms are expected through 
mid week under strong subsidence thanks to the subtropical high, 
with the exception being the far eastern high terrain. However, by 
Wednesday night, low level moisture ticks up with 1000-700 MB mixing 
ratios increasing to 10-12 g/kg. Enough instability, and this 
moisture in place, SC AZ lower elevations could develop isolated 
storms as early as Wednesday night. 

&&

.LONG TERM /THURSDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...    
Latest NBM/WPC guidance depicts the greatest coverage of Major 
HeatRisk across the forecast area on Thursday, with morning lows in 
the middle to upper 80s across the lower deserts and forecast highs 
106F-110F. These temperatures during the hottest time of the year 
may not prompt extreme heat headlines, but as we head into 
meteorological fall, daily normals drop off noticeably, resulting in 
more sensitive Major HeatRisk thresholds than what folks may have 
gotten accustomed to over the last few months. It also makes sense 
that Thursday would be the warmest of the next several days, as 
thermal profiles would have had more time to respond to the near 
climatological maximum strength ridge overhead. Heat indices will 
likely also be at their highest values, peaking between 108F-117F 
across the lower deserts. Temperatures then begin a gradual 
downtrend heading into the weekend as the subtropical high weakens 
and is displaced from overhead. 

As anticyclonic subsidence weakens, especially by late Thursday and 
into Friday, chances for lower desert thunderstorms become 
introduced across South-Central AZ (20-30%). A familiar monsoon 
thunderstorm evolution may begin to take place beginning Thursday 
and could last into the weekend, with afternoon thunderstorms 
focused over the eastern AZ high terrain, which will push outflows 
towards South-Central AZ in the evening that may be capable of 
sparking additional thunderstorms. Current thermodynamic profiles 
suggest all the typical monsoon thunderstorm hazards may come into 
play, including strong, gusty winds, blowing dust, localized heavy 
rain resulting in flash flooding, and frequent lightning. However, 
as we head into the weekend, the forecast confidence decreases 
substantially. WPC cluster analysis reveals large discrepancies, 
with close to 40% of ensemble members comprising a solution which 
shows negative midlevel height anomalies diving into the 
northwestern and north-central CONUS, possibly impacting the flow 
aloft as far south as the Desert Southwest and turning winds out of 
the west, beginning a drying trend. Other solutions comprise 
clusters which show subtropical ridging remaining in place somewhere 
near/over the Southwest US and keeping the influence of northern 
stream energy far enough north so as not to influence flow aloft 
significantly. Either way, drying will likely not be pronounced 
enough to preclude rain/thunderstorm chances once a sufficient 
forcing mechanism becomes introduced. Ensemble mean PWATs even 
remain near or above seasonal levels this weekend. Current NBM/WPC 
PoPs and QPF suggest higher/more widespread chances heading into 
Sunday, perhaps picking up on the influence of a distant/elongated 
shortwave trough axis rotating through from the Northwest US 
troughing that a good chunk of solutions show. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 2300Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
No major weather concerns will exist through Tuesday evening under 
occasional mid/high cigs. Winds will behave similarly to the past 24 
hours including a later than usual overnight switch to easterly, as 
well as limited afternoon gusts. 


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 
No major weather concerns will exist through Monday evening under 
periodically thick mid/high cigs. Winds will generally favor a west 
to northwest direction with very little gustiness and periods of 
light and variable conditions.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Temperatures will warm to above normal levels through the middle of 
the week. Afternoon minimum humidities will generally range between 
20-30% areawide through much of the week, with Tuesday expecting a 
larger area across the lower deserts between 15-20% before 
rebounding back near 20% Wednesday. Fair to good overnight 
recoveries are expected throughout the week. Fairly typical diurnal 
winds with occasional afternoon upslope breeziness can be expected 
through much of the week. Rain and thunderstorm chances will remain 
low and mostly limited to the eastern Arizona high terrain through 
midweek before slight chances become introduced to the lower deserts 
of at least the eastern districts during the latter half of the week.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Extreme Heat Warning from 10 AM Tuesday to 8 PM MST Thursday 
     for AZZ531-532-535>544-546-548>551-559.

     Extreme Heat Warning from 10 AM Wednesday to 8 PM MST Friday for 
     AZZ530-533.

CA...Extreme Heat Warning from 10 AM Tuesday to 8 PM PDT Friday for 
     CAZ562-566-567.

     Extreme Heat Warning from 10 AM Wednesday to 8 PM PDT Friday for 
     CAZ569-570.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Ryan
LONG TERM...Whittock 
AVIATION...18
FIRE WEATHER...Whittock/Ryan
